title: Scope network registry rollback to one job
summary: Replace whole-registry rollback with a per-job compare-and-set receipt that merges only the failed transition's state and inverse deltas.
reason: Remediate P1 AUDIT-FIND-W01-019. A failed done/release persistence or rerun-row compare-and-set could restore every registry collection, erasing unrelated concurrent claims and resurrecting completed jobs.
behavior_before: Done/release handlers deep-copied the entire registry before mutation and assigned every collection and counter back on rollback, regardless of mutations committed by other request or reaper threads.
behavior_after: Rollback captures one job, its source/worker/failure keys, and transition deltas. Restore uses source-owner compare-and-set, reinserts only that job, inverses only its counters and throughput, and preserves unrelated jobs, completions, worker evidence, late reports, and quarantines before persisting the merged state.
tests_added: tests/python/desktop/test_network_inflight_registry.py: target-only rollback preserves an unrelated completion, claim, worker statistics, late report, and quarantine; failed target completion preserves a later same-worker success; source-owner conflict refuses rollback without replacement.

tests/python/desktop/test_network_coordinator_http.py: barrier-driven Network CSV rerun done CAS failure interleaves an unrelated completion and new claim, then verifies both merged in-memory state and crash-recovered persisted state.

notes: Finding disposition: AUDIT-FIND-W01-019 is remediated and independently validated against current source, pre-fix red evidence, deterministic barrier-driven HTTP interleaving, direct target/source CAS conflict, same-worker completion merging, crash-recovered persisted state, the full network suite, and full desktop baseline classification. Python impact: coordinator registry rollback and HTTP done/release recovery only; request payloads, media policy, and source files are unchanged. Rollback refuses a changed target/source identity, subtracts only the failed completion's numeric contributions, conditionally restores target-owned failure evidence, and removes at most the first post-snapshot late report so later same-job evidence survives. Representative real-media validation is not required.
